title: Bouldy: visual app walkthrough
source: Current local frontend, sample data at 390 x 844. Production behaviour is not verified. Planned flows are discussion proposals.

items.title: Welcome
items.job: Introduce Bouldy and give a new or returning climber a clear way in.
items.rule: Signing in is required to open the journal. A successful sign-up also signs the user in.
items.question: Does this explain why a climber should use Bouldy?

items.title: Log in
items.job: Return to your own climbing journal.
actions: Submit or switch to Sign up
items.rule: There is no password-reset or OTP screen in this frontend. An error keeps the user on Log in.
items.question: What account-recovery journey must we add before a wider release?

items.title: Create an account
items.job: Create a climbing identity and begin a personal journal.
items.rule: Current grade is optional free text. The current flow does not ask for a preferred gym.
items.question: Should onboarding explain grades, privacy or gym selection?

items.title: Home
items.job: See a personal climbing snapshot and choose the next action.
items.rule: These are journal summaries. Missing history must not be shown as a trustworthy zero.
items.question: What is the single most useful thing to see when opening Bouldy?

items.title: Choose a gym
items.job: Find a wall and start a visit.
actions: Start a session from a gym row
items.rule: Gyms and routes are shared records; their permission model still needs team agreement.
items.question: How should users find the right gym as this list grows?

items.title: Add a gym
items.job: Add a missing gym without leaving the list.
actions: Save or close the bottom sheet
items.rule: This is a short task in a bottom sheet. Duplicate-gym prevention and who may create records need decisions.
items.question: Can any climber add a gym, or should submissions be reviewed?

items.title: Gym and route browser
items.job: Recognise routes on the wall and start climbing.
items.rule: Only active routes appear for new climbing. The gym leaderboard link opens a planned page.
items.question: Which route details do climbers need to identify a line reliably?

items.title: Find the right route
items.path: Gym, session and Climbs route browsers
items.job: Reduce a busy wall to a manageable set of routes.
actions: Filter by available colour, wall, status or gym
items.rule: Available filters depend on the screen and data. URL/session memory keeps the browsing context after logging.
items.question: Are grade, colour and wall enough, or do we need route numbers or photos?

items.title: Add a route at a gym
items.job: Create the shared route record that future sessions will use.
actions: Add route name, wall and setter
items.rule: This is a full-screen form. Competition classification is labelled coming soon; it is not a working switch.
items.question: Which fields are essential, and who should be allowed to create routes?

items.title: Edit a route
items.job: Correct a shared active route without crowding the list.
actions: Change grade, colour, wall, styles, name or setter
items.rule: The editor accepts active routes belonging to this gym. Retired-route history remains readable. Closing the form does not save edits.
items.question: Who can edit shared information, and how should incorrect edits be handled?

items.title: Add a route while climbing
items.job: Record a missing route and return to the active visit.
actions: Open Add route in a live session
Save and return to the same session
items.rule: The route belongs to the gym, not only this session. A completed session cannot use this add-route journey.
items.question: Should the new route be ready for an immediate first log?

items.title: Session journal
items.job: Review visits over time and resume the latest climbing context.
items.rule: Sessions are grouped by month with progressive reveal. /history redirects here.
items.question: What helps someone understand whether their climbing is improving?

items.title: Live session
items.job: Log climbing quickly between tries.
items.rule: Today and earlier visits stay separate. Routes already tried are projects or repeats; a new visit does not reset lifetime flash eligibility.
items.question: Can this be used with one hand between climbs?

items.title: Route actions and continuing projects
items.job: See previous effort and act on the route without losing the session.
actions: Add a try or mark Sent
items.rule: Sent changes the current outcome without adding an extra try to an existing log. If this is today's first try, Sent creates one try. Earlier sessions are not rewritten.
items.question: Do users understand today's count versus their total effort?

items.title: First-try Flash
items.job: Record a first-ever successful try when complete journal history supports it.
actions: Open a route never tried before
Or log +1 for an unsuccessful try
items.rule: Unavailable or conflicting history suppresses Flash. These FE safeguards do not replace backend enforcement.
items.question: Should flash mean first ever try, and how do we explain that consistently?

items.title: Correct a live route log
items.job: Fix a mistaken attempt count or result.
items.rule: Correction edits the recorded summary; it does not add a physical try. Result/count correction is not available after a session ends.
items.question: Should ended sessions allow corrections? If so, what rules should apply?

items.title: Private route notes
items.path: Route sheet or route history > note editor
items.job: Remember beta or how a route felt for the next visit.
actions: Save independently of the climb result
Cancel without changing the saved note
items.rule: This is plain private text attached to the visit's route log. It is not a public review, felt-grade rating or session-wide note.
items.question: What do climbers actually want to remember after a try?

items.title: End a session
items.job: Finish the visit and record its length.
items.rule: The current interface uses a positive duration to identify an ended session. An explicit lifecycle/timer is separate backend work.
items.question: Do we need automatic timing, manual length, or both?

items.title: Completed session review
items.job: Look back at what was logged during one visit.
actions: Browse only routes logged that visit
Open route details and private notes
items.rule: No new attempts, route creation or result/count corrections are offered here. Private notes remain editable. Retired logged routes remain visible.
items.question: Which post-session summary would be worth revisiting or sharing later?

items.title: Climbs collection
items.job: See the routes you have ever logged, grouped by gym and grade.
items.rule: Best result, total tries and visits are derived from owned journal records. Grades are grouped within each gym.
items.question: Is a route collection or a visit diary the more useful default?

items.title: Your route history
items.job: Understand work on one stable route across multiple visits.
actions: Read total tries and send status
items.rule: Entries are session summaries, not a per-try timeline. The exact ordering of visits on the same date is unknown.
items.question: Which progress details are missing: felt grade, first-send date or something else?

items.title: History after a wall reset
items.job: Keep a climber's effort visible after the physical route disappears.
actions: Review old logs and private notes
items.rule: A similar name, colour or grade does not make a new wall-set the old route. Historical counts must stay attached to the old ID.
items.question: Who tells Bouldy when a wall is reset, and who retires the routes?

items.title: You: personal account
items.job: Review your own identity, activity and places you climb.
actions: Read account details and current grade
Review personal totals and visited gyms
items.rule: Email is shown only on this owner screen. Profile editing, public profile and privacy settings are placeholder destinations.
items.question: What should belong to a private account versus a public climbing identity?

items.title: Explore: community menu
items.job: Show the planned community directions without inventing social activity.
actions: Open feed, climber search, rankings, challenges or groups plans
Return to your working session journal
items.rule: The menu is built; the community services behind it are not. There are no real social metrics or fake rows.
items.question: Which one community feature would make the journal more valuable?

items.title: Edit profile
items.job: Proposed: edit a climbing display name, bio and profile photo.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs owner profile fields, validation and update APIs; avatars also need media storage.
items.question: Which identity fields are essential for the first release?

items.title: Public profile
items.job: Proposed: control the identity and selected statistics other climbers see.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs a separate public response and enforceable visibility rules. Do not expose the owner email or private notes.
items.question: Should profiles be discoverable, link-only or private by default?

items.title: Privacy and sharing
items.job: Proposed: choose discoverability, ranking participation and sharing.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs stored visibility settings and backend enforcement, plus blocking/reporting decisions.
items.question: Which privacy choices must exist before the first social feature?

items.title: Climbers' sessions
items.job: Proposed: see sessions friends deliberately share.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs sharing/follow relationships, privacy filtering and a feed service. Private journals must not become public automatically.
items.question: Would users want a feed, or simpler links to share a session?

items.title: Find climbers
items.job: Proposed: find opted-in climbers and open their public identity.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs visibility-filtered search and public-profile APIs; no user search works here yet.
items.question: How should people find friends without exposing private accounts?

items.title: Leaderboards and points
items.job: Proposed: compare results fairly, starting within a gym.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs scoring, eligibility, periods, ties, trusted result timing and ranking APIs. Global comparison additionally needs defensible gym-grade mapping.
items.question: What behaviour should points reward, and is competition a priority now?

items.title: Challenges
items.job: Proposed: join a goal with clear rules and a time window.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs challenge definitions, joins, progress, time windows and verification/reset rules. Gym-run challenges may need operator tools.
items.question: What is the smallest challenge people would actually join?

items.title: Groups and leagues
items.job: Proposed: climb with a private crew and compare across a season.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs membership, invitation permissions, roles, seasons and private standings.
items.question: Do we want informal groups first, or competitive leagues?

items.title: Route photos and beta videos
items.job: Proposed: recognise a line and reveal climbing beta when wanted.
actions: Today: read the plan and return to the parent screen
Future journey below is a proposal, not a working control
items.rule: Needs authorised persistent media storage, upload/link policy, processing, attribution and moderation. No upload or playback flow is implemented here.
items.question: Would one route photo or saved video links solve most of the immediate need?

items.title: Missing data and recovery
items.path: Owner journal/history when a read fails
items.job: Show what is known without inventing totals.
items.rule: A failed request is not an empty session. Duplicate records also make totals uncertain and may pause logging. The capture shows a sample read failure, not a production outage.
items.question: What information and recovery action should a climber see when saving or loading fails?

items.title: First-use empty state
items.job: Explain how a new climber can build their journal.
items.rule: This is a deliberately empty sample account state, not failed history.
items.question: Should first use guide people into one simple logged route?

items.title: Missing page
items.job: Give a useful way back from an invalid link.
items.rule: Home resolves according to sign-in state. /history is a compatibility redirect, not a separate page.
items.question: Where might shared or old links break, and how should we recover?
